History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
31-year-old man with history of eczema presents with a 3–4-day history of intensely pruritic, sore, cracked erythematous rash on chest, hands, and antecubital fossae, likely eczema flare; topical high-potency steroid, emollients, stronger antihistamine, trigger diary, and 1-week follow-up arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Very itchy, sore, red skin rash.  
• Onset/duration: Began 3–4 days ago; progressively persistent; interferes with sleep, work focus, and leisure activities (e.g., hiking).  
• Location: Chest, hands, inner elbows; no face involvement.  
• Character/progression: Erythematous, dry, cracked areas; no bleeding, pus, or discharge.  
• Prior episodes: Previous eczema limited to arms; prior prescribed cream and shower product worked then, but not effective this episode.  
• Self-treatment to date: OTC steroid cream (name, dose/route/frequency not documented) started last night—ineffective. OTC antihistamines (names/doses not documented)—ineffective.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies fever, systemic illness, respiratory or urinary symptoms. Bowels normal.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Frequent showers give temporary relief; no known new products or clothing changes; triggers unspecified.  
• Review of systems: Otherwise negative per conversation.

Past Medical History:
• Atopic dermatitis/eczema – prior diagnosis, recurrent; previous topical therapy.  
• Asthma – childhood/past; currently asymptomatic and off treatment.  

Medications:
• None regular.  
• OTC topical steroid cream – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• OTC antihistamines – names/doses not documented.  

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Age 31; lives with several flatmates to save money.  
• Employment: Project manager at a pharmaceutical company (full-time).  
• Tobacco: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: “A few beers per week”; previously higher intake when younger, now moderate.  
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.  

Family History:
• Not discussed/not documented.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not documented.  
• Skin (from tele-visual inspection per provider): Erythematous rash with dry, cracked areas; distribution chest, hands, antecubital fossae; appears consistent with eczematous dermatitis (exact morphology details not provided).  
• Other systems: Not examined/not documented.

Investigations:
• None performed or ordered during consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected eczema flare (widespread pruritic, erythematous dermatitis)  
  • Prescribe higher-potency topical corticosteroid (specific agent/strength not documented).  
  • Prescribe emollient for bath/shower use; advise regular moisturization.  
  • Prescribe oral antihistamine Fexofenadine (dose/frequency not documented) for pruritus; consider trial of alternative antihistamines if needed.  
  • Advise daily application of steroid and emollient for 7–10 days before reassessment.  
  • Counsel on potential triggers; start diary of products, clothing, activities.  
  • Recommend avoiding potential irritants, limiting hot showers, and maintaining skin hydration.  
  • Follow-up: Return in 1 week if no improvement or sooner if worsening.  
  • Safety-net: Seek immediate care for spreading rash, infection signs (pus, fever), or systemic symptoms.

General plan items: None additional.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected: Vitals, detailed skin description, complete medication list with doses, complete allergy list (food/environmental), vaccination status.  
• Internal conflicts: Onset described as “a few days,” “three days,” and “four days” (conflict noted).  
• Transcript quality: Audio intermittently poor; some speech unclear but key clinical information obtainable.
